title: Generic descriptive sensory evaluation of cooked Mozambique tilapia (Oreochromis mossambicus) fillets fed diets containing Hermetia illucens larvae meal
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Although fish fed diets containing alternative protein sources often exhibit good growth performance, the inclusion of these proteins in aquafeeds raises consumer concerns about potential changes in fillet aroma, appearance, flavour, and texture, which may influence overall sensory acceptability. This study evaluated the effects of dietary inclusion of black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) larva (BSFL) meal at 0, 200, 300, and 400 g kg−1 on the nutritional composition and sensory attributes of Mozambique tilapia (Oreochromis mossambicus). Proximate composition and fatty acid profiles were analysed using methods of the Association of Official Analytical Chemists, and the sensory attributes of cooked fillets were assessed using a ten-point line scale.

RESULTS

Dietary BSFL inclusion altered fillet moisture and ash content and increased the saturated fatty acid content of tilapia, whereas eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) content did not differ significantly (P > 0.05) among dietary groups. Appearance descriptors showed no significant differences. Earthy aroma peaked at 300 g kg−1 BSFL inclusion. The spicy flavour was most intense at 300 g kg−1 in comparison with the other diets. At 400 g kg−1 inclusion, fillets exhibited the highest scores for mushiness and mouth coating, suggesting compromised textural characteristics.

CONCLUSION

Dietary BSFL meal inclusion significantly affected the moisture, ash, and fatty acid content, and the sensory attributes of cooked O. mossambicus fillets. The findings demonstrated sensory limitations associated with high BSFL inclusion levels, highlighting the need for balanced feed formulations that optimise both nutritional value and sensory appeal. © 2026 The Author(s).
